references.text: The fifth commandment commands us to honor father and mother, which is the basis for the command to fear parents in Lev 19:3.
The command to keep the Sabbaths is repeated here, with emphasis on the Sabbath as a sign between God and Israel.
The fourth commandment about keeping the Sabbath day holy, which parallels the command to keep the Sabbaths.
Repetition of the command to honor father and mother in Deuteronomy.
The Sabbath command in Deuteronomy, which elaborates on the meaning of keeping the Sabbaths.
Proverbs urges us to listen to a father's instruction and not reject a mother's guidance.
An exhortation to listen to one's father and not despise one's mother when she is old.
The same chapter repeats the command to keep the Sabbaths and to fear God's sanctuary.
Repeats the command to keep the Sabbaths and to have reverence for the sanctuary.
Paul quotes the command to honor father and mother as the first commandment with a promise.
Children are urged to obey their parents in everything, for this is pleasing to the Lord.
Jesus refers to the command to honor father and mother and criticizes the Pharisees for setting it aside.
Jesus mentions the command to honor father and mother as part of the commands one must keep.
Refers to reverence for our earthly fathers, as a parallel to reverence for God.
